title: User Perceptions of the Lentera Learning Platform: Reanalysis of a Custom Usability Questionnaire
abstract: This study re-examines user perceptions of the Lentera learning platform using the 30-response, ten-item questionnaire dataset embedded in the source manuscript. The original report applied the alternating System Usability Scale (SUS) scoring rule and obtained 49.16, although all ten administered statements are positively worded and therefore do not match the directionally alternating SUS instrument. Recalculation reproduces the original arithmetic as 49.1667 but confirms that the value cannot be interpreted as a valid SUS score. Direct analysis of the 300 original responses yields an overall mean of 3.40 on the five-point scale, a respondent-level median of 3.45, and an exploratory Cronbach's alpha of 0.944. Item means range from 3.10 for the usefulness of error messages to 3.60 for perceived search efficiency. The strongest corrected item-total relationship is observed for overall satisfaction, while error handling remains the clearest descriptive area for follow-up. These results support a moderate, generally favorable perception of the platform in this sample, but they do not establish task effectiveness, objective efficiency, or a standardized usability grade. The paper therefore distinguishes custom-survey evidence from SUS benchmarking and outlines a more defensible evaluation design for future Lentera studies.

title: Unlocking Human Capital Development through Technopreneurship Education: Evidence on the Moderating Influence of Entrepreneurial Mindset from Niger State, Nigeria
journal: Elicit Journal of Economics and Management Studies
abstract: Purpose: Graduate unemployment remains a persistent challenge in Niger State, Nigeria, despite growing investments in entrepreneurial education. This study examines the moderating effect of entrepreneurial mindset (EMS) on the relationship between technopreneurship education and human capital development (HCD) among tertiary institution students. Methodology: A quantitative research design was adopted using data from 500 students selected from a population of 9,135 students across tertiary institutions in Niger State through purposive sampling. The study assessed key dimensions of technopreneurship education—Business and Financial Literacy (BFL), Entrepreneurial Skills (ES), Innovation and Creativity (IC), and Technological Competence (TC). Data were analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM), with EMS specified as a moderating variable. Results: The findings indicate that BFL (β = 0.194, p = 0.002), ES (β = 0.218, p = 0.001), IC (β = 0.146, p = 0.004), and TC (β = 0.224, p = 0.000) exert significant positive effects on HCD. Although EMS shows only a marginal direct effect on HCD (β = 0.092, p = 0.054), it significantly strengthens the relationships between TC and HCD (p = 0.000) and between BFL and HCD (p = 0.006). Novelty and contribution: The study advances technopreneurship literature by demonstrating that entrepreneurial mindset enhances the effectiveness of specific technopreneurial competencies in driving human capital development. Practical and social implications: The study recommends integrating entrepreneurial mindset training into technopreneurship curricula, supported by mentorship and experiential learning initiatives, to improve graduate employability and foster sustainable human capital development in tertiary institutions.

title: Multivalent antiviral conjugates enhance activity against Influenza via cross-linking viruses
abstract: Abstract Long-acting drug–Fc conjugate (CD388) has emerged as a new class of antivirals against influenza A and B, yet the mechanisms governing how Fc conjugation reshapes small-molecule function remain undefined. Here we establish a programmable multivalent antiviral conjugates (AVCs) platform by click chemistry that enables flexible combination of valencies and conjugated drugs, allowing systematic interrogation of valency-dependent antiviral mechanisms. Using zanamivir as a model, mono-, di-, and trivalent zanamivir are conjugated with Fc, with trivalent zanamivir-Fc conjugates (AVC-Z3) exhibiting higher activity than lower-valent AVCs. AVC-Z3 induces inter-virion aggregation, thereby coupling blockade of viral entry with restriction of viral release. This cross-linking–mediated dual-stage inhibition represents a mechanistic shift from neuraminidase suppression to physical viral immobilization. Furthermore, trivalent peramivir-Fc conjugate (AVC-P3) is synthesised and exhibits stronger antiviral activity than AVC-Z3 in vitro, with much longer half-life in vivo than AVC-Z3, and CD388 with YTE mutation. The in vivo antivirus efficacy of AVC-P3 surpasses other AVCs, baloxavir, and CD388 in H1N1-, H3N2-, H5N1-, and influenza B-infection mice models. Together, our findings define ligand valency as a determinant of antiviral mechanism.

title: From Resources to Performance: How Social and Intellectual Capital Drive MSME Innovation
journal: Shirkah: Journal of Economics and Business
abstract: Micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) operate under persistent resource constraints, making the effective mobilization of intangible resources increasingly important for sustaining business performance. This study examines how social capital and intellectual capital contribute to MSME performance and investigates whether innovation serves as a mechanism through which these resources are transformed into business outcomes. It also examines the role of managerial ability in strengthening the relationship between social capital and MSME performance. Drawing on Resource-Based Theory, the study employed a quantitative explanatory design involving 204 ultra-micro food and beverage entrepreneurs. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS. The findings demonstrate that social capital contributes to both innovation and MSME performance, while intellectual capital strengthens innovation and has a particularly important contribution to performance. Innovation also functions as a significant pathway linking both social capital and intellectual capital with MSME performance. Managerial ability contributes directly to performance but does not significantly moderate the social capital–performance relationship. These findings indicate that MSME performance depends not simply on possessing relational and knowledge-based resources, but on the capacity to mobilize and transform these resources through innovation and effective managerial action. The study extends the resource-based perspective by highlighting innovation as a critical resource-conversion mechanism in ultra-micro enterprises.

Toward Evidence‐Based ESG Reporting: The Added Value of Geospatial and Satellite Data
abstract: ABSTRACT This study addresses the limitations of conventional ESG reporting, including reliance on self‐reported and third‐party data, lack of standardization, and limited verifiability, by examining how geospatial data enhance disclosure quality. It aims to synthesize and critically evaluate existing research on satellite and geospatial data in ESG reporting in order to identify dominant research directions and unresolved challenges. It employs a systematic bibliometric analysis of Scopus‐indexed publications, complemented by thematic mapping and cluster identification, to explore the structure and evolution of the literature. The findings demonstrate that geospatial data enhance environmental performance measurement, enable asset‐level monitoring, and strengthen risk assessment, thereby mitigating information asymmetries. Nevertheless, the diffusion of these data remains constrained by coverage gaps, methodological inconsistencies, and governance issues. Standardization and interoperability challenges can be tackled through stronger global governance and structured public‐private collaboration that aligns data production with concrete user needs in sustainable finance, agriculture, and environmental management.
